name: Cooks Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of cutaneous syndactyly primarily involving the third and fourth fingers
Brachydactyly affecting the fourth and fifth toes
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with variable expressivity
Normal cognitive development without associated intellectual disability

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic syndactyly and brachydactyly with a positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing may be supportive but no specific gene identified.

imaging: Radiographs showing soft tissue syndactyly and brachydactyly of distal phalanges
No bone fusion or complex osseous anomalies
genetic: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern observed in families
No specific gene mutation identified to date
other: Clinical diagnosis based on phenotypic features and family history

distinguishingFeatures: More severe limb malformations including aplasia or hypoplasia of bones
May have different inheritance pattern and associated anomalies

redFlags: Presence of bone fusion rather than cutaneous syndactyly
Associated systemic malformations or intellectual disability
Progressive limb deformities or functional impairment
references: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Syndactyly
Fryns JP, et al. Familial syndactyly: clinical and genetic aspects. Am J Med Genet. 1990
